verdict.rationale: Penpot documents an official, agent-agnostic MCP server that lets AI agents read and interact with design files. It also offers an API with extensive access to objects and properties, backed by a published OpenAPI document, and its AI workflows mention connecting tokens to implementation. However, the specific design-context elements the story names are not shown as retrievable through the MCP server. Missing for 10: documented MCP/API retrieval of frames/boards, variables/tokens, rendered screenshots, and component-to-code mappings, plus hands-on or independent corroboration of agent-driven implementation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my coding agent can pull real design context — frames, variables, screenshots, component mappings — through an MCP server or API to implement the design

citations.quote: In Penpot, design is expressed as code, so AI agents can easily read and interact with your design files creating high-fidelity artifacts.
Penpot MCP server is agnostic and enables high-quality multi-directional AI workflows through our world-class open plugin API.
Get extensive access to objects and properties to enable external rendering, workflow automation, enhanced app functionality, and more.
Penpot enables plenty of AI workflows, from generating editable design structures to connecting product logic, tokens, and implementation.
